documents.section: Cost Accounting Period Statuses and Transaction Accounting
documents.text:
• Pending Close: The Pending Close status works similar to the Open status and doesn’t include any additional
validations. However, when a period is in the Pending Close status, any new transaction that falls in or before
the period won't be staged in Cost Accounting or Receipt Accounting. After the period is closed or reopened,
these new transactions will be processed. You can use the Pending Close status to hold transactions from being
accounted in a given period.
Any transactions entered before the pending close date will be processed, even if they're in an error state.
Transactions created after the pending close date, even if they relate to a current or prior period, won't be
processed. Revenue lines, COGS recognition, and manual cost adjustments will continue to be processed even
after the period is set to Pending Close.

documents.section: Cost Accounting Period Statuses and Transaction Accounting
documents.text:
• Pending Close: The Pending Close status works similar to the Open status and doesn’t include any additional
validations. However, when a period is in the Pending Close status, any new transaction that falls in or before
the period won't be staged in Cost Accounting or Receipt Accounting. After the period is closed or reopened,
these new transactions will be processed. You can use the Pending Close status to hold transactions from being
accounted in a given period.
Any transactions entered before the pending close date will be processed, even if they're in an error state.
Transactions created after the pending close date, even if they relate to a current or prior period, won't be
processed. Revenue lines, COGS recognition, and manual cost adjustments will continue to be processed even
after the period is set to Pending Close.

cells: Verify a coordinated journey from home to transportation, parking, campus entrance, public interior routes, destination identification, staff assistance, and the return journey using consistent names, landmarks, maps, directories, graphics, lighting, and digital content.
Readiness window: July 8-25, 2025 | First-day monitoring: July 28, 2025 | Public office hours: Monday-Friday, 8:00 a.m.-4:30 p.m.
Controlled source: International Health Facility Guidelines 2023 Part W: Wayfinding Guidelines, published by TAHPI. Treat wayfinding as the complete journey, not only interior signs.
Open actions remain owner- and date-specific. Yellow cells indicate an item requiring active follow-up before first-day operations.

source_context.projection: Original 45 control rows and all original checklist columns; noncontrol lines retained separately

values.Required Wording / Check: Confirm clinic name, appointment details, preparation, destination landmark, cancellation or rescheduling route, and staffed navigation help.
Map shows 1810 Albion Street, parking approach, public entrance, elevator or stairs, destination, and return route.
values.Evidence / Verification Date: Draft proof v3.2; field check pending

values.Required Wording / Check: Use the five exact service names, floors, and distinct landmarks; include office hours and navigation-help escalation.
Plain-language reminder states the clinic, floor, landmark, arrival guidance, and how to cancel or reschedule.
values.Exception Notes: Schedule with owner before the July 25 readiness close.

values.Required Wording / Check: Verify 1810 Albion Street pin, public entrance, drop-off, accessible parking, and transit approach.
Confirm clinic relocation directional sign is visible before the final turn into patient parking.
values.Evidence / Verification Date: Draft proof v1.1; field check pending

values.Required Wording / Check: Direct patients from accessible spaces to the public entrance without crossing restricted service lanes.
Verify lighting supports sign legibility from parking through the public entrance after early morning arrival.
values.Exception Notes: Schedule with owner before the July 25 readiness close.

values.Required Wording / Check: Entrance sign identifies Nashville General Hospital Main Campus and directs relocated-clinic patients to registration.
Separate public routes from loading, staff-only, and clinical restricted areas using consistent graphics.
values.Evidence / Verification Date: Draft proof v2.0; field check pending

values.Required Wording / Check: Directory uses current service names, exact floors, and Laboratory, NHC Eye Clinic, and Orthopedics Clinic landmarks.
Map shows public elevators, stairs, registration, restrooms, relocated services, and return route to the lobby.
values.Exception Notes: Schedule with owner before the July 25 readiness close.

values.Required Wording / Check: Staff repeat the approved service, floor, and landmark wording and offer escort or escalation when needed.
Direct ENT patients to the second floor near the Laboratory.
values.Evidence / Verification Date: OPEN ACTION — upload corrected proof after owner field check

values.Required Wording / Check: Elevator directory lists ENT on the second floor near the Laboratory.
Directional blade identifies ENT and the Laboratory landmark without routing through restricted areas.
values.Exception Notes: Schedule with owner before the July 25 readiness close.

values.Required Wording / Check: Destination sign reads ENT and matches the directory and appointment wording.
Return route directs patients to public elevators, main lobby, parking, and Albion Street exit.
values.Evidence / Verification Date: Draft proof v1.3; field check pending

values.Location / Channel: Main lobby to first-floor east corridor
values.Required Wording / Check: Direct Nashville General Hospital Rheumatology Clinic patients to the first floor near the NHC Eye Clinic.
Directory lists Rheumatology near the NHC Eye Clinic and preserves the full clinic name in patient-facing detail.
values.Exception Notes: Schedule with owner before the July 25 readiness close.

values.Required Wording / Check: Temporary insert and permanent sign both read Rheumatology; verify mounting, contrast, and lighting.
Explain August 2025 operational relocation and continuity-team assignment without changing the approved landmark wording.
values.Evidence / Verification Date: Draft proof v2.2; field check pending

values.Required Wording / Check: Checkout map directs patients back to the lobby, accessible route, parking, and Albion Street.

source_context.system: Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM Cost Management 26B
source_context.projection: All source work_orders, cost_periods and work_order_cost_events rows; precise source policy excerpt

documents.section: Cost Accounting Period Statuses and Transaction Accounting
documents.text:
• Pending Close: The Pending Close status works similar to the Open status and doesn’t include any additional
validations. However, when a period is in the Pending Close status, any new transaction that falls in or before
the period won't be staged in Cost Accounting or Receipt Accounting. After the period is closed or reopened,
these new transactions will be processed. You can use the Pending Close status to hold transactions from being
accounted in a given period.
Any transactions entered before the pending close date will be processed, even if they're in an error state.
Transactions created after the pending close date, even if they relate to a current or prior period, won't be
processed. Revenue lines, COGS recognition, and manual cost adjustments will continue to be processed even
after the period is set to Pending Close.

result.prompt:
The September 2025 month-end close team is reviewing manufacturing cost activity in Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM Cost Management 26B for Modine's Racine operation. Please investigate the cost activity associated with the work order for the September manufacturing order ending in 1070 and determine whether any event was created after the September cost period entered Pending Close.

Your final response must identify the relevant work order and source transaction, state the event's amount, give the exact event-created time and the exact Pending Close time, calculate how late the event was, report its recorded accounting status, and conclude whether that status is consistent with Oracle's documented Pending Close treatment for newly created transactions. Keep the review read-only and do not change any database records.

amount_cents.description: Integer USD cents, not a dollar amount.

late_minutes.description: Event-created time minus Pending Close time, in minutes.

status_consistent.description: Whether the recorded status is consistent with the supplied Oracle policy for this event type and timing.

documents.section: Cost Accounting Period Statuses and Transaction Accounting
documents.text:
• Pending Close: The Pending Close status works similar to the Open status and doesn’t include any additional
validations. However, when a period is in the Pending Close status, any new transaction that falls in or before
the period won't be staged in Cost Accounting or Receipt Accounting. After the period is closed or reopened,
these new transactions will be processed. You can use the Pending Close status to hold transactions from being
accounted in a given period.
Any transactions entered before the pending close date will be processed, even if they're in an error state.
Transactions created after the pending close date, even if they relate to a current or prior period, won't be
processed. Revenue lines, COGS recognition, and manual cost adjustments will continue to be processed even
after the period is set to Pending Close.

answer.explanation: The component-issue event falls in Sep-25 and was created 4,500 seconds (75 minutes) after that period entered Pending Close. Oracle 26B states that new transactions created after Pending Close and falling in or before that period will not be staged or processed until the period is closed or reopened. The recorded POSTED status is inconsistent with this treatment. This INPUT event is not within the revenue-line, COGS-recognition or manual-cost-adjustment exceptions.

oracle_policy.section: Cost Accounting Period Statuses and Transaction Accounting
oracle_policy.rule: New transactions falling in or before a Pending Close period are not staged in Cost Accounting or Receipt Accounting and are processed after close or reopen. Transactions entered before Pending Close continue to process, including errors. Revenue lines, COGS recognition, and manual cost adjustments continue processing after Pending Close.
oracle_policy.application: An ordinary manufacturing transaction created after Pending Close should be held from staging/processing; event type and recorded status are needed before concluding consistency.
